content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To sign up for little league, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Submit the final registration packet to the league office (10 minutes)
Step 2. Research local league boundaries and eligibility (1 hour)
Step 3. Attend the mandatory parent orientation meeting (2 hours)
Step 4. Buy a new baseball glove (45 minutes)
Step 5. Get a physical exam from the pediatrician (1 hour)
Step 6. Attend the player evaluation and skills clinic (3 hours)
Step 7. Purchase the team-specific uniform pants and belt (30 minutes)
Step 8. Register for the tryout time slot online (15 minutes)
Step 9. Fill out the medical history questionnaire (20 minutes)
Step 10. Pay the seasonal registration fee (5 minutes)
Step 11. Sign the liability waiver and code of conduct (10 minutes)
Step 12. Join the league's private social media group (5 minutes)
Step 13. Receive the official team practice schedule (10 minutes)
Step 14. Order the personalized team jersey (15 minutes)
Step 15. Verify residency with a utility bill (10 minutes)
Step 16. Upload the residency verification to the portal (15 minutes)
Step 17. Locate the player's original birth certificate (30 minutes)
Step 18. Watch the league safety training video (45 minutes)
Step 19. Meet the assigned team coach (30 minutes)
Step 20. Scan the residency documents into a PDF (10 minutes)
Step 21. Complete the online player profile (20 minutes)
Step 22. Download the league communication app (5 minutes)
Step 23. Sign up for the team snack rotation (5 minutes)
Step 24. Volunteer for a field maintenance shift (2 hours)
Step 25. Review the league's equipment requirements (15 minutes)
Step 26. Sync the league calendar to your phone (5 minutes)
Step 27. Submit a photo for the player ID card (5 minutes)
Step 28. Purchase a protective batting helmet (30 minutes)
Step 29. Buy a pair of baseball cleats (40 minutes)
Step 30. Gather proof of residency documents (20 minutes)
Step 31. Buy a gear bag to hold equipment (20 minutes)
Step 32. Visit the local sporting goods store (30 minutes)
Step 33. Create an account on the league website (15 minutes)
Step 34. Buy a regulation-size baseball for home practice (5 minutes)
Step 35. Label all equipment with the player's name (20 minutes)
Step 36. Check for available league scholarships or discounts (30 minutes)
Step 37. Attend the first team practice (90 minutes)
Step 38. Read the league rulebook (1 hour)
Step 39. Confirm the league's age division requirements (15 minutes)
Step 40. Receive the team assignment notification (1 day)
Step 41. Purchase a bat that meets USA Baseball standards (45 minutes)
Step 42. Check the league's official calendar for key dates (20 minutes)
Step 43. Sign up for the league newsletter (5 minutes)
Step 44. Research the best bat sizes for the player's age (30 minutes)
Step 45. Schedule the doctor's appointment (10 minutes)
Step 46. Buy a protective cup and sliding shorts (15 minutes)
Step 47. Double-check the entire application for errors (15 minutes)
Step 48. Purchase baseball socks in team colors (10 minutes)
Step 49. Introduce yourself to other team parents (20 minutes)
Step 50. Request a copy of the player's school enrollment form (2 days)
Step 51. Photocopy the birth certificate (5 minutes)
Step 52. Buy a water bottle for the season (10 minutes)
Step 53. Submit the completed medical clearance form (5 minutes)
Step 54. Receive the league's "Ready to Play" confirmation email (1 hour)
Step 55. Purchase the required league-branded hat (15 minutes)
Step 56. Update the player's emergency contact information (10 minutes)
Step 57. Receive the evaluation results (2 days)
Step 58. Finalize the volunteer background check (3 days)
Step 59. Gather all medical and identification paperwork (1 hour)
Step 60. Check the league's fundraising requirements (30 minutes)
